source: NCERT Class XI, Statistics for Economics, Ch. 4 (Presentation of Data).

sections.heading: 1. Ways of Presenting Data
points: Organised data can be **presented** in three ways: **textual (paragraph), tabular (tables), and diagrammatic (graphs/diagrams)**.
Presentation makes data attractive, easy to understand and compare.

sections.heading: 2. Tabular Presentation
points: A **statistical table** arranges data in rows and columns.

sub: **Table number, title, head note, captions (column headings), stubs (row headings), body, footnote, source note**.

points: Tables allow systematic comparison and condense large data.

sections.heading: 3. Diagrammatic Presentation

sub: **Bar diagrams** — simple, multiple, sub-divided (component) bars; compare magnitudes.

points: Diagrams give a quick visual impression but are less precise than tables.

sections.heading: 4. Graphic Presentation (Frequency Data)
points: **Histogram** — bars for continuous class intervals (area = frequency).
**Frequency polygon** — line joining mid-points of the tops of histogram bars.
**Ogive (cumulative frequency curve)** — 'less than' and 'more than' curves; their intersection gives the **median**.
**Time series (line) graph** — shows a variable over time (arithmetic line graph).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Table parts: title, captions (columns), stubs (rows), body, footnote, source.
Bar diagram, pie diagram, pictogram = diagrammatic.
Ogive intersection ('less than' & 'more than') gives the median.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Captions = column headings; stubs = row headings** of a table.
A **histogram** is for **continuous** data (bars touch); a bar diagram has gaps.
An **ogive** is a **cumulative frequency curve**; its two curves intersect at the **median**.
